summary.headline: PG Electroplast Q2 FY27 revenue rose 42.5% YoY to Rs 934 crore, with EBITDA up 54.8% to Rs 69.14 crore at a 7.4% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue reached Rs 934 crore (+42.5% YoY), and H1 consolidated revenue crossed Rs 2,950 crore for the first time. Growth came from both volume (double-digit in Room AC) and price, as commodity costs and rupee depreciation were passed through to customers. Gross contribution percentage fell YoY, which management attributed to pass-through pricing, a mix shift toward low-margin electronics and memory-driven price spikes, while per-unit margins were said to be stable. Management kept FY27 Room AC volume guidance at about 20% to 25%, with the compressor plant in Supa and the Sri City refrigerator plant on track.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 483.4 crore; JV EBITDA Rs 22.7 crore vs Rs 10.3 crore

segments.name: Room AC
segments.commentary: H1 revenue Rs 1,561 crore (+36.2%), with volume growth about 22% and the rest from price. FY27 volume guided at 20% to 25% (about 2.1 to 2.2 million units vs 1.7 million in FY26); Q3 volume growth seen in early-to-mid teens and Q4 stronger.

segments.name: Washing machine
segments.commentary: H1 sales above Rs 500 crore (+60.7%). FY27 growth guided at about 40% to 50%, with full-year revenue close to Rs 1,000 crore.

segments.name: Electronics
segments.commentary: H1 growth of 90.3% to 12% of revenue, driven mainly by memory-driven price increases in TV motherboards. FY27 revenue guided at Rs 500 to 600 crore (target about Rs 550 crore); H2 growth expected to be volume-led and slower.

segments.name: Plastic molding and components
segments.commentary: H1 revenue Rs 521.6 crore, up 7.5%. Cooler sales grew only 4.8% to Rs 19.3 crore as channel destocked after high-cost inventory built up in the prior year.

segments.name: Goodworth Electronics (JV)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue Rs 623.8 crore vs Rs 483.4 crore, and EBITDA Rs 22.7 crore vs Rs 10.3 crore. FY27 guided at Rs 800 to 900 crore, with the TV season slowing in H2.

guidance_outlook: Room AC full-year FY27 volume growth about 20% to 25% (management: 20% plus or minus 2% to 3%); Room AC revenue above Rs 4,000 crore said to be possible.
Average realisation increase for FY27 about 15%, including a further price increase from January 2027.
Second-half margins expected to be slightly better than H1, helped by seasonality, operating leverage and PLI booking in Q4.
Other operating costs expected to rise in line with volume growth of about 20% to 25%, not with revenue growth.
Incentives for FY28 estimated at about Rs 105 to 110 crore: about Rs 60 crore PLI at PG Technoplast, NGM PLI about Rs 20 crore, and state incentives of about Rs 28 to 30 crore a year.
FY27 capex guided at about Rs 400 crore, largely done; FY28 capex about Rs 150 to 200 crore.
Gross margin percentage may stay low even in H2 because of higher commodity costs, since AC bill of material rose from about Rs 14,000 to about Rs 18,500 per unit.
capex_capacity: Supa compressor plant: trial production by end of November 2026, mass production from January-February 2027, targeting 1.5 million+ compressors in CY27 (1.5 to 1.8 million per Q&A); decision on second line in April-May 2027.

Sri City refrigerator plant: 1.2 million units capacity, commercial production targeted in Q4 FY27 (trial production January-February 2027), with FY28 production of about 700k units; Phase 1 direct cool and side-by-side, Phase 2 frost-free and multi-door.
Salarpur, Bhiwadi campus operational; some Greater Noida operations relocating there (coolers, sanitaryware, plastic components, mould making).
Super compressor unit: margin figures to be shared at production start, expected around end of Q3 FY27.
Refrigerator compressor line at Sri City to be decided after refrigerator production stabilises.
demand_pricing: Management described secondary sales in Room AC as strong and channel inventory as lower than last year; primary sales were muted in Q2 due to the GST transition in August and a late September start.
Price increases were taken in January, April and October 2026, with a further hike planned from January 2027 based on the average cost of October to December.
Gross margin percentage fell because of commodity pass-through (copper, aluminium, plastic), rupee depreciation, and a mix shift toward electronics, where memory-chip prices rose sharply.
Industry Room AC growth expected at more than 15% for FY27, per brand estimates cited by management.
Cooler channel destocked after high-cost inventory; plastic makes up about 65% to 70% of cooler bill of material.
Exports limited to small volumes to SAARC nations; pricing versus Chinese and European suppliers was described as a major challenge.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall, and is there under-absorption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin % is lower in a high-commodity environment because contract manufacturing earns a fixed amount per unit. Mix (electronics, low margin) and memory-driven price spikes also reduced the percentage, while per-unit margins are in the usual range.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Room AC volume in Q2 and the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Absolute quarterly numbers were not given; Q2 volume was described as flat YoY. Full-year FY27 volume growth is guided at 20% to 25%, to about 2.1 to 2.2 million units.

qa_highlights.question: Cost trajectory and H2 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower Q2 other expenses reflected about Rs 5 crore lower forex loss and about Rs 3 crore of one-offs not repeated. Costs are expected to rise with volume (20% to 25%), and H2 margin is expected to be slightly better than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher commodity prices raise inventory and working capital needs. Management expects H2 interest cost not to rise significantly from H1, since capex is already paid.

qa_highlights.question: Electronics revenue and Goodworth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Electronics FY27 target Rs 500 to 600 crore (about Rs 550 crore). Goodworth FY27 guided at Rs 800 to 900 crore, with the TV season slowing in H2 after a steep price-driven rise.

qa_highlights.question: PLI and incentive outlook for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the Rs 105 to 110 crore estimate for FY28, comprising PG Technoplast PLI (about Rs 60 crore), NGM PLI (about Rs 20 crore), and state incentives (about Rs 28 to 30 crore a year at PG Technoplast).

risks_watch: Gross margin percentage remains compressed while commodity costs and electronics mix stay high; watch whether the January 2027 price increase restores it.
Q3 FY27 volume growth is guided at only early-to-mid teens, so the full-year 20% to 25% target depends on a strong Q4 and on secondary sales.
Working capital and inventory rose, which keeps interest cost elevated.
Compressor ramp-up (1.5 to 1.8 million units in CY27) and Sri City refrigerator start (Q4 FY27) carry execution and approval risk.
Electronics growth is largely price-led (memory chips), so H2 growth is expected to normalise.
POS machine project is stalled due to customer-side issues, with no progress.
Possible slowdown in rural and semi-rural demand; management said AC is largely urban and sees no near-term challenge through March 2027.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the order book and on FY27 volume and capex execution, but defensive on margins, repeatedly redirecting to per-unit economics. Cautious on Q2 primary sales and on exports, and vague on some numbers (e.g., Sept 2024 inventory, Q2 AC volume).
key_quotes: Growth in first half came from combination of volume and price.
And as you all know, on a per-unit basis, margin remains stable and we get a fixed amount on a per -unit basis and not the percentage margin for doing the contract manufacturing.
So, don't look at this business as a percentage margin business, because that is not the way internally we track.
Because we are going to utilize large part of the capacity for in-house only, So it will be margin accretive.

growth.why: Management held FY27 Room AC volume growth at 20-25% (about 2.1-2.2 million units vs 1.7 million), with Supa compressor and Sri City refrigerator plants in trial runs for CY27/Q4 FY27 ramp, backed by price increases (~15% average realisation) and washing machine guidance of 40-50%; Q2 RAC volume was flattish, so near-term delivery depends on H2 ramp.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides H2 EBITDA margin slightly better than H1's 7.4%, helped by seasonality, operating leverage and PLI booking of close to Rs 70 crore in Q4, though gross margin % may stay low on commodity costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Supa compressor plant is in trial production by end-Nov 2026 with mass production Jan-Feb 2027 targeting 1.5m+ compressors in CY27, and Sri City refrigerator plant (1.2m units capacity) targets commercial production in Q4 FY27 with 700k FY28 output.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 Room AC volume guided at 20-25% (about 2.1-2.2m units vs 1.7m), but Q2 was flat YoY and Q3 is only early-to-mid teens, so the full-year target needs a strong Q4.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of about Rs 400 crore is largely done and FY28 capex is about Rs 150-200 crore; a decision on a second compressor line is set for April-May 2027 and the refrigerator compressor line at Sri City awaits stabilisation.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 RAC volume at 20-25% and Rs 800-900 crore for Goodworth, and said only that RAC revenue above Rs 4,000 crore is possible, with no explicit raise signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 RAC volume guided at only early-to-mid teens and H2 electronics growth expected to slow after a 90.3% H1 rise, so the 20-25% volume target depends on a strong Q4.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sri City refrigerator plant is set for commercial production in Q4 FY27 with Phase 1 direct cool and side-by-side models, and Phase 2 frost-free and multi-door models follow.

rows.label: Further price hike from January 2027
rows.why: Average realisation up about 15% in FY27 including a further hike from January 2027, after hikes in January, April and October 2026, to offset AC bill of material rising from about Rs 14,000 to Rs 18,500 per unit.

rows.label: FY28 incentives of Rs 105-110 crore
rows.why: Management confirmed Rs 105-110 crore for FY28: about Rs 60 crore PG Technoplast PLI, about Rs 20 crore NGM PLI, and state incentives of about Rs 28-30 crore a year.

rows.label: Washing machine growth 40-50% in FY27
rows.why: H1 washing machine sales rose 60.7% to above Rs 500 crore, with full-year FY27 revenue guided close to Rs 1,000 crore (40-50% growth).

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, FY27 capex and compressor/refrigerator ramp, but defensive on the falling gross margin, repeatedly pointing to per-unit economics; analysts pressed on margins, working capital, and the Q2 flat volume.
